pages.text: A magnet sticks to the fridge door. It holds my picture up.
A magnet pulls some things towards it. We cannot see the pull, but we can feel it.
Magnets pull things made of iron and steel. A paper clip is made of steel. So is a nail.
A magnet does not pull wood, paper, plastic or glass.
A magnet does not pull every metal. Kitchen foil is made of aluminium. A magnet does not stick to it.

quickWords.th: อะลูมิเนียม

pages.text: Every magnet has two ends called poles. One is the north pole. One is the south pole. In our pictures, north is red and south is blue.
Put a north pole near a south pole. The two magnets pull together. Snap!
Put two north poles together. They push each other away. Two south poles push away too.
Inside a piece of iron are many tiny magnets. In a magnet they all point the same way. That is what makes its pull strong.
A magnet pulls hardest at its two ends. Look where the paper clips hang.

quickWords.th: คลิปหนีบกระดาษ

pages.text: A magnet can pull through paper. Move the magnet under the page and the paper clip follows.

quickWords.th: เคลื่อนไปตาม

pages.text: A paper clip that touches a magnet can lift another paper clip. For a little while, it is a magnet too.

quickWords.th: คลิปหนีบกระดาษ

pages.text: The Earth is a giant magnet. A compass needle is a small magnet. It turns to point north.
Magnets pull iron and steel. Different poles pull together. Same poles push apart. Never put a magnet in your mouth. What will your magnet stick to?
